name: PROLACTIN
description: Prolactin is a pituitary hormone that regulates lactation and has multiple physiological roles. This test measures prolactin levels using chemiluminescent immunoassay. Elevated prolactin can cause galactorrhea, amenorrhea, and infertility. The test helps diagnose pituitary tumors and other hormonal disorders.

testdetails.instrumentation: Abbott Architect, Roche Elecsys, Beckman Coulter

literatureReview: Prolactin is secreted by lactotroph cells in the anterior pituitary gland and has diverse physiological roles beyond lactation. The test uses immunometric chemiluminescent assays for accurate measurement. Normal range is 2-20 ng/mL for non-pregnant adults, with slight variations by sex and age. Hyperprolactinemia (>20 ng/mL) can cause galactorrhea, amenorrhea, infertility, and reduced libido. Common causes include prolactinomas, medications (antipsychotics, antidepressants), hypothyroidism, and stress. Macroprolactin (biologically inactive prolactin-IgG complexes) can cause falsely elevated results. Morning sampling is preferred, and strenuous exercise should be avoided before testing. Results should be interpreted with clinical symptoms and may require pituitary imaging if persistently elevated.
